definition: Short-term memory your device uses while running apps. More RAM means smoother multitasking, but it doesn't make a single app run faster on its own.
How much space you have to keep photos, apps, and files. Unlike RAM, storage keeps its contents even when the device is off.
The chip that does the actual computing. Newer/higher-tier processors handle demanding tasks (gaming, editing) faster and often more efficiently.
A screen type where each pixel lights itself, giving true blacks and strong contrast, usually at the cost of slightly higher price than LCD.
How many times per second the screen redraws (measured in Hz). Higher refresh rates (90Hz, 120Hz) make scrolling and animations look smoother.
For phones, measured in mAh (capacity). For laptops, usually quoted as hours of use, since runtime depends heavily on the processor and screen.
The wattage a device can accept determines how fast it refills. 65W charges much faster than 18W, but requires a compatible charger.
The core software a device runs on — iOS, Android, Windows, macOS — which determines its app ecosystem and update schedule.
A measure of an engine's power output. Higher horsepower generally means quicker acceleration and higher top speed, but isn't the whole picture — torque matters too.
A measure of an engine's twisting force — how strongly it can get a vehicle moving from a stop or pull while loaded, distinct from horsepower.
Continuously Variable Transmission — a gearbox with no fixed gear steps, giving smooth, stepless acceleration instead of the usual gear shifts you feel.
The system that transfers engine power to the wheels. Manual requires the driver to shift gears; automatic (or CVT) does it for them.
How far a vehicle travels per unit of fuel — commonly km/l here. Higher numbers mean fewer fuel stops and lower running costs.
Safety devices that inflate on impact to cushion occupants. More airbags (front, side, curtain) generally means broader crash protection.
Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems — features like lane-keep assist, automatic emergency braking, and adaptive cruise control that help prevent or soften collisions.
Which wheels receive the engine's power: FWD (front), RWD (rear), or AWD (all four) — this affects handling, traction, and typically fuel economy.
How far the seat sits off the ground on a motorbike — shorter riders typically want a lower seat height for confident flat-footing at stops.
The gap between the lowest part of a vehicle and the road — higher clearance handles rough roads/speed bumps better.
Electric Vehicle — powered by a battery and electric motor instead of (or alongside, for hybrids) an internal combustion engine.
